items.title: Earl Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002
items.q: Then in 1972 we had another president Jerry Spain. He ascended to the presidency.

ctx.x: So Pop Kennedy passed away in 1967 then we had another president, kind of a weak president. Kennedy was a strong labor man. He knew all the delegates from our various labor councils and he was on the Executive Board of the American Federation of Musicians. He was a strong labor man. Then when he passed Al Arnold ascended. Al wasn’t very assertive. And so then in 1972 we had another president Jerry Spain. He ascended to the presidency. He had gone to law school and he became president. Well he didn’t like Oakland.…

Local 424 was the Richmond Local, 510 was the San Leandro Local. And many of the fellas held dual membership. So they considered that Oakland office their office.
